# Radio state fixtures

Authentic `iw` and `batctl` output, captured 2026-08-31 from `mac80211_hwsim` on
the lab development machine, for the `RadioState` reader's tests.

**These are `SIMULATED`, not a hardware capture.** `mac80211_hwsim` produces
real, ABI-faithful `iw` and `batctl` output -- the text a real driver produces --
but there is no radio behind it. The MAC addresses are randomly generated by
hwsim per run and are not real hardware identifiers, so `SECURITY.md`'s
scrub-before-commit rule does not apply; nothing here came from a real node.

A capture from real hardware, when one exists, belongs beside these with the node
identifier, capture date and image build recorded, per `docs/evidence/README.md`.
It would test the same parser against a real vendor driver's output, which is the
thing hwsim cannot stand in for.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `iw-dev.txt` | `iw dev`: one mesh-point interface, its type and address |
| `iw-station-dump-associated.txt` | `iw dev wlan0 station dump`: one established mesh peer |
| `iw-station-dump-empty.txt` | the same, with no peers: `iw` prints nothing |
| `batctl-originators.txt` | `batctl meshif bat0 originators`: one originator over the mesh |
